title: Stephen Hawking Threw a Party for Time Travellers ⏳ #shorts
cast: a cheerful cartoon professor in a high-tech wheelchair, glasses, neat grey suit (respectful, friendly)

lines.say: A famous scientist threw a party, and nobody came. That was the whole point.
shots: an empty elegant party room with balloons, champagne glasses and a banner, {hero} waiting alone
close-up of party glasses and canapes untouched on a table

lines.say: In 2009, Stephen Hawking decorated a room at Cambridge University, with balloons, snacks and champagne.
shots: old stone college buildings of Cambridge at golden hour, bicycles outside
{hero} next to a table full of champagne glasses and snacks, smiling

lines.say: There was a banner saying, welcome time travellers. But he didn't send out any invitations.
shots: a big banner over a doorway in a party room, balloons, warm light, no readable letters
{hero} with a sly smile next to a closed door

lines.say: He only sent the invitations after the party was over.
shots: an elegant invitation card with a gold clock on it on a desk, quill pen
a postman putting a glowing invitation into an old post box at night

lines.say: His idea was simple. If time travel is possible one day, someone from the future could read it, and come back.
shots: a glowing swirling time portal opening in the middle of the party room
a futuristic traveller in a silver suit peeking out of the portal, curious

lines.say: He waited for hours. Nobody showed up.
shots: a clock on the wall with its hands spinning fast, the empty party room
{hero} alone at the party late at night, balloons drooping

lines.say: He joked that this was experimental evidence that time travel isn't possible.
shots: {hero} laughing with a chalkboard full of equations behind him
a deflated balloon lying on the floor next to an empty champagne glass

lines.say: So if you ever get a strange invitation from the future, just remember that
shots: the glowing invitation card floating among stars and galaxies
{hero} raising a glass toward the camera, warm candle light

description:
True story: Stephen Hawking threw a party for time travellers, and sent the invitations after it ended.

Would you have gone? Tell us in the comments.

In 2009 Stephen Hawking held a party for time travellers and only sent the invitations afterwards. Nobody came. A true story he described in his TV series Into the Universe.

Sources: Discovery Channel 'Into the Universe with Stephen Hawking'; University of Cambridge.

Made with AI-assisted pictures and voice.
